newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 2.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - July 2.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and People News.
PARIS - Connect World, the multimedia unit of Havas Advertising, says Citroen, a unit of PSA Peugeot Citroen, has chosen it to create and run its site on the
Internet's World Wide Web.(Reuter)

PARIS - Bernard Kouchner, France's new Health Minister, says he will introduce new requirements for health warnings on cigarette packets and will not tolerate an alcohol brand using the World Cup football tournament as a shop window.(Reuter)
PARIS - Free newspaper group Spir Communication and marketing group High Co. form an alliance in couponing, a direct marketing technique recently arrived in France. (Les Echos)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

PARIS - Shares in French pay television group Canal Plus rose four percent on Tuesday, building on strong recent gains on expectations the group will get control of Telepiu in Italy, analysts say. (Reuter)
PARIS - French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn promises aid to promote the development of multimedia in France, but says this will be primarily aimed at creators, not consumers.
(Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
PARIS - Car sales in France fell 30.7 percent last month, the worst June performance since 1962, as price-cutting failed to entice anxious consumers, industry officials say. (Reuter)

PARIS French holding company Euris, the main shareholder in Moulinex, would lower its stake in the appliance maker to seven percent from an indirect 33 percent under a planned restructuring of the group's capital, French daily Les Echos says.(Reuter)

PARIS - The chairmen of LVMH and British merger partners Guinness and Grand Metropolitan may bury the hatchet on Wednesday if they can agree on a way to blend their drinks businesses, analysts say.(Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS
PARIS - Bruno Le Moult, 46, vice chairman and creative director of Young & Rubicam Paris, died on Monday.(Le Figaro)

PARIS - Anne Sinclair, who gave up her prominent Sunday evening political programme following the appointment of her husband, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, as finance minister, has been appointed deputy managing director in charge of news strategy and development at TF1. (Les Echos)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
